title: DSX | Workload Structure
description: Follow observed workload phases and explore current workload, component, instance, replica-group and Pod attribution with optional resource measurements.

options.content: Select an exporter job, namespace and workload. The timeline shows observed phase intervals; the graph shows current attribution and optional resource measurements. Load `recording-rules.yaml` for inventory and attribution. Metric Samples contains raw evidence.

panels.title: Selected workload
panels.description: Published identities remain when status or age is unavailable. Age requires agreement across reporting replicas. Published definition describes emitted metadata. Phase summary requires all nine agreed flags and available scrapes. See raw samples for invalid observations and disagreements.

panels.title: Phase history | status at each observed time
panels.description: Each row is an independent phase flag. Colored intervals name the matching phase; gray intervals mean that phase did not match. Hover an interval for its start and end times. Several phases can match at once. Gaps mean unavailable, invalid or disagreeing samples. Times reflect sampled observations at the query resolution, not exact lifecycle event timestamps.

options.content: Graph: orange = workload, blue = component, purple = instance, gray = replica group, green = Pod. Node values: GPU utilization / VRAM used (GiB). Click a node for CPU, memory and identity details. Select optional cAdvisor and DCGM jobs to add measurements. N/A means no accepted measurement.

panels.title: Workload structure | GPU, memory and CPU
panels.description: Published attribution, not ownerReferences or desired replicas. Node labels show names and types. Inside each node: maximum measured GPU utilization and GPU memory (VRAM) used in GiB. Click a node for CPU cores, working-set memory and identity details. Resource measurements are optional. Missing or rejected telemetry stays unavailable; nodes remain visible. VRAM totals count each UUID/MIG entity once per node. They describe device memory use, not per-process allocation. Solid edges show attribution; dashed edges show logical replica-group membership. Colors identify object types, not health.

panels.title: Exact accepted Pod attribution
panels.description: Every label from the conflict-checked recording rule is retained. Only observation_valid=true rows are shown. This table includes a standalone Pod even when its graph uses the root node. Blank labels are not inferred.

panels.title: Raw status, creation and failure evidence
panels.description: Unaggregated target rows expose disagreement, validity and failure reasons. Creation values are Unix seconds; status values are independent phase flags. Scrape success does not prove reevaluation.
